title: The Unexpected Postcard
premise: Ada Okafor, a single father who fled a scandalous academic career seven years ago, runs the only bookshop in the fading orchard town of Marrow Creek. When a postcard arrives naming him co-heir to the abandoned Hollis orchard alongside Ruth Calloway—the woman whose testimony once destroyed him—he learns the deed cannot be split and the orchard will be sold unless both heirs sign within ninety days. Forced into partnership, Ada and Ruth unearth the truth of what really happened the night his career ended, discovering her silence was bought by the same man now pressuring them to sell. In the end, Ada chooses truth over safety: he testifies, keeps the orchard with Ruth as a community press and reading garden, and finally lets himself belong—to the town, to his daughter's future, and to Ruth.
about_author: P. M. Winterbourne is a former small-town bookseller who writes quiet romances about second chances and stubborn places. They live at the edge of an old orchard with two cats and a growing collection of unsent postcards.

chapters.title: The Postcard That Wouldn't Be Filed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Seven years into careful invisibility—bookshop, daughter Nia, no photographs online—a postcard arrives from a probate lawyer naming him heir to the Hollis orchard. He burns it in the back-room kettle burner but memorizes every word. Emotional beat: dread cracking open a life built on small safe steps.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Deed
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth Calloway, orchard-town native turned estate attorney, receives the same summons and recognizes the second name with a jolt she hides even from herself. She drives past the bookshop twice without going in. Emotional beat: guilt wearing the mask of professionalism.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The lawyer explains the deed's stubborn clause: joint heirs must jointly decide within ninety days or the land goes to developer Aldous Vane, the man who bankrolled Ada's downfall. First face-to-face meeting with Ruth in the dusty orchard house; old fury and something warmer collide. Emotional beat: enemies forced into proximity.

chapters.title: What Nia Found in the Attic
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Nia, eleven and curious, finds a box of letters in the orchard attic between Ruth's grandmother and Ada's late mentor—evidence the two families were once entwined. Ruth and Ada agree to a truce to read them together. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance kindled by shared history neither knew.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Flashbacks braided with present: how Vane offered Ada redemption and silence in exchange for burying research fraud that would have implicated Ruth's family. Ada took the deal and ran. Now Vane reappears in Marrow Creek, offering the same bargain. Emotional beat: the cost of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. A storm strands Ada and Ruth pressing apples in the old cider barn; over cheap wine she admits her testimony was coerced—that Vane threatened her grandmother's deed. The letters confirm it. They almost kiss, then Ada pulls away, unable to trust anything built on lies. Emotional beat: intimacy and betrayal entangled.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Burns Bright
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Vane escalates: anonymous complaints threaten the bookshop's lease, and Nia overhears adults whispering about her father's 'scandal.' Ada, terrified of losing Nia's belief in him, nearly signs the sell agreement alone. Emotional beat: rock bottom—the safe life collapsing anyway.

chapters.title: Truth Is a Door You Open Together
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth publicly files the original fraud evidence with the county, burning her own family's reputation to free Ada from the old bargain. She tells him: loyalty without truth isn't loyalty. Ada realizes staying invisible was never really an option—and never really living. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframing love.

chapters.title: The Hearing at Harvest Time
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Climax. At the county hearing on the deed, Ada testifies to everything—his silence, Vane's coercion, the letters—while Ruth stands beside him and Nia watches from the gallery. Vane's hold collapses under documented proof. The judge upholds the joint deed. Emotional beat: courage as public act, not private endurance.

chapters.title: Where the Orchard Meets the Page
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, closing with Ruth's letter. Spring: the orchard reopens as a community press and reading garden, the bookshop thriving, Nia planting the first tree. Ada and Ruth, unhurried now, write their own first entry in the orchard ledger. Emotional beat: belonging chosen freely—the price paid, the harvest begun.
